source: sgtestpaper.com free test papers, P5/P6 Science, 2022-2025 (P5 2022 not hosted at the guessed address)

patterns.name: Characteristics of living and non-living things
patterns.structure: A statement or short list about what living things need or do, or a set of items to sort into living and non-living.
patterns.skill: Recall what living things need and do; tell living from non-living.

distractorTraps.description: an option swaps what a living thing needs (water, food, air) with what it does (grow, respond, reproduce)
an option treats movement or growth-like change as proof of life (a car, a flame)

patterns.name: Classify organisms into broad groups (plants, animals, fungi, bacteria)
patterns.structure: A classification chart, key or table of features (spores, seeds, fur, scales, six legs) with a question on where an organism belongs or which placement is wrong.
patterns.skill: Place organisms in groups from observable features; read a classification chart or key.

distractorTraps.description: an option gives a feature that only some members of the group have
insects, reptiles or amphibians are swapped because they share one feature
fungi are filed with plants

patterns.name: Properties and uses of materials
patterns.structure: An object or a results table (strength, absorbency, flexibility) and a question on which material suits a purpose or which property explains a use.
patterns.skill: Match a material property to a use; read a results table.

distractorTraps.description: a real property of the material that is irrelevant to the use named
the row with the highest or lowest value is read for the wrong property

patterns.name: Life cycle stages and comparison (insect, amphibian, plant)
patterns.structure: A cycle diagram with stages labelled by letter, or two animals compared, with questions on which stage feeds, moults, flies or looks like the adult.
patterns.skill: Order and compare life cycle stages; tell complete from incomplete metamorphosis.

distractorTraps.description: pupa and nymph are swapped, so the wrong metamorphosis is assigned
a behaviour is given to a stage it does not belong to (a pupa eating)
the wrong animal is said to have young that look like the adult

patterns.name: Cell parts, functions and continuity of kind
patterns.structure: A plant or animal cell diagram, a table of which cell parts are present, or an inherited-trait table, with a question on function or presence.
patterns.skill: Name cell parts and functions; recognise that traits pass from both parents.

distractorTraps.description: cell wall or chloroplast is said to be in animal cells
the functions of nucleus and cytoplasm or cell membrane are swapped
an inherited trait count ignores that both parents contribute

patterns.name: Plant reproduction: flower parts, pollination, fertilisation, dispersal, germination
patterns.structure: A flower, fruit or seed diagram with letters, or a table of features of wind- and insect-pollinated flowers, with questions on function, order of events or which flower can form a fruit.
patterns.skill: Link flower parts to function; sequence pollination, fertilisation, dispersal and germination.

distractorTraps.description: pollen landing on the stigma is called fertilisation, or the reverse
the roles of stigma, anther and ovary are exchanged
a fruit feature (wing, hook, juicy flesh) is matched to the wrong agent
sunlight or soil is listed as a germination need

lineartKinds: flower, fruit and seed drawings with lettered parts

patterns.name: Human reproduction: gametes, fertilisation and development
patterns.structure: A diagram of the male and female reproductive systems with lettered parts, or a statement about fertilisation and the developing baby.
patterns.skill: Identify the reproductive organs, gametes and where fertilisation and development happen.

distractorTraps.description: the roles of ovary, uterus and testis are swapped
fertilisation is placed in the uterus rather than the oviduct
the egg cell and the fertilised egg are confused

lineartKinds: male and female reproductive system drawings

patterns.name: Properties of solids, liquids and gases (mass, volume, shape)
patterns.structure: A set-up with air pumped in or a stone dropped into water, or a table of two properties for several substances, asking what happens to mass and volume.
patterns.skill: Compare mass, volume and shape of solids, liquids and gases; show that gas takes space and has mass.

distractorTraps.description: air is said to have no mass or no definite volume
mass and volume are swapped when air is added to a closed container
a liquid is said to keep its shape

svgKinds: experimental set-up (syringe, tank, balloon, measuring cylinder)

patterns.name: Changes of state: melting, freezing, boiling, condensation, evaporation
patterns.structure: A diagram of arrows between ice, water and steam, a melting and boiling point table with a state at one temperature, or a heating or cooling graph.
patterns.skill: Name the change of state and its heat direction; read melting-point tables and heating curves.

distractorTraps.description: condensation and evaporation, or melting and freezing, are exchanged
heat loss is attached to a change that needs heat gain
the state is read against the melting point only, ignoring the boiling point

patterns.name: Rate of evaporation: factors and fair set-ups
patterns.structure: Several set-ups that differ in surface area, temperature or wind; pick the fair pair or explain which dries faster.
patterns.skill: Choose a fair set-up for a factor that changes the rate of evaporation.

distractorTraps.description: the pair differs in more than one factor
a bigger water amount is taken to evaporate faster

patterns.name: Water cycle and water conservation
patterns.structure: A cycle diagram with lettered stages, or everyday actions to sort into saving and wasting water.
patterns.skill: Order the stages of the water cycle and link each to a change of state; choose water-saving actions.

distractorTraps.description: a stage of the cycle is matched to the wrong change of state
an action that sounds thrifty uses more water in total

patterns.name: Plant parts and their functions (root, stem, leaf, stomata)
patterns.structure: A plant with lettered parts, or a set-up in which a part is covered or removed, with questions on function and what would happen.
patterns.skill: Match a plant part to its function; predict what happens when a part is covered or removed.

distractorTraps.description: roots and stem, or leaf and stem, are given each other's functions
water is said to enter through the leaf
stomata are said to take in water or to close in the light

patterns.name: Human digestive system: organs and digestion
patterns.structure: A digestive system diagram with lettered organs, or a table matching organ to function, or the order food passes through.
patterns.skill: Order the digestive organs and state what each does.

distractorTraps.description: the roles of stomach and small intestine, or liver and pancreas, are swapped
absorption of digested food is placed in the large intestine
two organs are listed in the wrong order

lineartKinds: digestive system drawing with lettered organs

patterns.name: Respiratory and circulatory systems (lungs, heart, blood)
patterns.structure: A diagram of lungs, heart and body with arrows showing oxygen-rich and oxygen-poor blood, or a table comparing inhaled and exhaled air.
patterns.skill: Trace air and blood through lungs, heart and body; compare inhaled and exhaled air.

distractorTraps.description: the vessel carrying oxygen-rich blood is named as carrying oxygen-poor blood
the functions of heart and lungs are exchanged
inhaled and exhaled air composition is swapped

lineartKinds: lungs and heart with blood paths

patterns.name: Gases in air and tests for gases
patterns.structure: A candle burning in a closed jar, a limewater test or a statement on what air contains.
patterns.skill: Recall the composition of air and interpret burning and limewater tests.

distractorTraps.description: air is said to be mostly oxygen
burning is said to use up carbon dioxide

patterns.name: Plant transport system: water and food transport
patterns.structure: A stem stained with coloured water, a ring of bark removed from a stem, or a diagram of arrows for water and food in a plant.
patterns.skill: Explain how water and food move through a plant from a stained stem or ringed stem.

distractorTraps.description: water is said to move down and food only up
water-carrying and food-carrying tubes are exchanged
the part above the ring is said to die first when it is the part below

svgKinds: stained stem and ringed stem set-up

patterns.name: Electric circuits: complete and open circuits, symbols, switches
patterns.structure: Circuit diagrams with cells, bulbs and switches; decide which bulbs light, which circuit is complete, or what a switch controls.
patterns.skill: Decide which bulbs light or whether a circuit is complete from a diagram.

distractorTraps.description: a bulb in a parallel branch is said to go out when its neighbour fails
a bulb is said to light with a switch open
a wire that bypasses a bulb is ignored

svgKinds: circuit table of bulbs lit or not

patterns.name: Current strength, conductors and insulators
patterns.structure: A test circuit with a gap for an object, or two circuits with different numbers of cells or bulbs, asking which bulb is brighter or which material conducts.
patterns.skill: Predict bulb brightness from cells and bulbs; classify conductors and insulators from a test.

distractorTraps.description: adding bulbs is said to brighten them
a metal-looking object is called a conductor without the test result

patterns.name: Magnets: poles, magnetic materials, attraction and repulsion
patterns.structure: Bar magnets with poles marked, or discs and rods tested against a magnet, asking which attract, which repel or which must be a magnet.
patterns.skill: Predict attraction or repulsion from poles; identify magnets and magnetic materials from tests.

distractorTraps.description: like poles are said to attract
an object attracted by a magnet is said to be a magnet itself
the test for a magnet (repulsion) is confused with attraction

patterns.name: Forces and their effects (push, pull, contact and non-contact forces)
patterns.structure: A moving object, ramp or hurdle scene, or a list of effects of a force, asking which force acts or what the force does.
patterns.skill: Identify the force acting and its effect on motion or shape.

distractorTraps.description: a force is said to change the mass of an object
gravity or magnetic force is listed as a contact force
a constant speed is taken to need a continuing force

patterns.name: Friction, elastic spring force and weight: investigations
patterns.structure: A spring with loads, a surface comparison for friction, or a graph of extension against load.
patterns.skill: Interpret friction, spring-extension and weight investigations.

distractorTraps.description: friction is drawn in the direction of motion
weight in newtons is confused with mass in grams
the elastic spring force is drawn pointing away from the stretched spring

patterns.name: Food chains and food webs: energy flow and population effects
patterns.structure: A food web with lettered organisms, with questions on which statement is false, who is a producer or predator, or what happens to populations when one changes.
patterns.skill: Trace energy flow and predict population changes in a food web.

distractorTraps.description: the arrow is read as "eats" instead of "energy goes to"
only the first effect on a population is considered
a prey increase is said to follow a predator increase

patterns.name: Organism, population, community and habitat
patterns.structure: A habitat description, a list of organisms or a table of conditions, asking which term applies or what a habitat provides.
patterns.skill: Distinguish organism, population, community and habitat.

distractorTraps.description: population (one kind) and community (all kinds) are swapped
habitat is taken to mean the animals living in it

patterns.name: Adaptations of plants and animals (structural and behavioural)
patterns.structure: An animal or plant with a feature described, asking what the adaptation is for or whether it is structural or behavioural.
patterns.skill: Match an adaptation to its purpose; classify structural and behavioural adaptations.

distractorTraps.description: a body feature is labelled behavioural or the reverse
the purpose of the feature is matched to another adaptation

lineartKinds: animal feet, beaks and plant parts

patterns.name: Human impact on the environment and conservation
patterns.structure: A list of actions, asking which conserve resources or which cause pollution or loss of habitat.
patterns.skill: Judge the effect of human activity on the environment; choose conservation actions.

distractorTraps.description: an action that sounds green causes more harm overall
pollution is linked to the wrong effect on the community

patterns.name: Light: sources, seeing, reflection and shadows
patterns.structure: A light source, object and screen drawn in a row, or a ray path in a periscope, asking what is seen, the shadow shape or the mirror position.
patterns.skill: Decide what can be seen and how a shadow changes; follow a ray path.

distractorTraps.description: moving the object towards the light is said to shrink the shadow
a reflecting object is called a light source
a transparent object is said to cast a full shadow

svgKinds: source, object and screen ray diagram

patterns.name: Heat gain and loss, temperature and thermometers
patterns.structure: Two objects at different temperatures, a cooling or warming graph, or a scene such as a jacket or an ice pack, asking the direction of heat flow.
patterns.skill: Tell heat gain from heat loss; separate temperature from heat; read thermometers and graphs.

distractorTraps.description: cold is said to travel into the warm object
a hotter object is said to contain more heat
a jacket is said to make heat

patterns.name: Effects of heat: expansion and contraction, and heat conductors
patterns.structure: A metal lid, a rod or a ball-and-ring set-up, asking what expands or contracts and why a lid loosens, or which material conducts heat best.
patterns.skill: Use expansion and contraction to explain observations; compare heat conductors.

distractorTraps.description: a metal is said to expand when cooled
the best heat conductor is picked from the wrong end of the results

patterns.name: Respiration and the Sun as the source of energy
patterns.structure: A statement or short chain on what respiration needs and gives, or how energy in fuel and food came from the Sun.
patterns.skill: State what respiration needs and gives; trace energy back to the Sun.

distractorTraps.description: the two processes are swapped
an animal is said to get energy straight from the Sun

patterns.name: Photosynthesis: requirements, products and experiment set-ups
patterns.structure: A leaf covered with foil, a plant in the dark or an iodine-tested leaf, asking what the plant needs or makes.
patterns.skill: Identify what a plant needs and makes; interpret leaf-test set-ups.

distractorTraps.description: oxygen is listed as a need and carbon dioxide as a product
a leaf that stays brown with iodine is read as having starch
plants are said to take in their food from soil

patterns.name: Energy forms and conversion
patterns.structure: A device (bell, toy car, ball on a track) or a list of energy sources and forms, asking for the order of conversions or which statement is wrong.
patterns.skill: Name energy forms and trace the conversions in a device.

distractorTraps.description: energy is said to be lost or destroyed when an object stops
food energy or fuel is labelled kinetic
the order of conversions is reversed

patterns.name: Fair test and experiment design: variables and set-up choice
patterns.structure: A table of set-ups differing in a few factors, asking which set-ups to compare, which variable to change, keep the same or measure, or the aim of the experiment.
patterns.skill: Choose which set-ups to compare; name the variable changed, kept the same and measured.

distractorTraps.description: the pair differs in more than one factor
the measured variable and the changed variable are swapped
the aim claims more than the set-up can show

patterns.name: Interpret a graph or results table and draw a conclusion
patterns.structure: A line graph, bar chart or table of results, asking for a reading, a trend, a prediction or the valid conclusion.
patterns.skill: Read values and trends from a graph or table; pick the valid conclusion.

distractorTraps.description: the conclusion goes beyond the range of the data
the value is read from the wrong axis or the wrong row
two changes that go together are said to cause each other
